entities.summary: John Gabriel Stedman was a Dutch-British army officer and writer best known for writing The Narrative of a Five Years Expedition against the Revolted Negroes of Surinam (1796). This narrative covers his experience in Suriname between 1773 and 1777, where he was a soldier in a Dutch regiment deployed to assist colonial troops fighting against groups of maroons. He first recorded his experiences in a personal diary that he later rewrote and expanded into the Narrative. The Narrative was a bestseller of the time and, with its firsthand depictions of slavery and other aspects of colonialism, became an important tool in the fledgling abolitionist movement.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Narrative of a Five Years Expedition against the Revolted Negroes of Surinam provided firsthand accounts of slavery and colonialism, contributing to the growing abolitionist movement in Europe. Its impact can be seen in the increased public awareness of the horrors of slavery, leading to calls for reform and eventual emancipation.
